title: `time`: durations, timers, tickers and time zones

videos.script: Every lesson so far has slept, timed or waited. This one opens the package that does it. {{duration}} A duration first. It looks like a number with a unit. It is a count of nanoseconds with a type of its own, and the type refuses an int that has none. {{mono}} Then the two clocks inside every reading of the time. One can jump when somebody corrects it. The other only moves forwards, and that is the one an interval uses. {{timers}} Timers and tickers next. A timer is a sleep you can wait on in a select, and cancel. A ticker fires over and over, and a reader who is late finds one tick waiting, not a pile of them. {{zones}} Last, places. One meeting, printed in four cities, is still one instant. And a date is formatted with a date: the second of January, two thousand and six. {{close}} Lesson 21 turns command-line flags into values, durations included.
